"},{"insert":"Card Advantage"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The deck is efficient, not infinite. If the major engines do not appear, resources have to be spent carefully. Do not confuse controlling the game with having unlimited cards. You do not.

Losing the Gun"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Heliod is difficult to remove permanently. Walking Ballista is not. Protect the card that actually kills people. Fortunately, Triskelion, tutors and Agatha's Soul Cauldron mean losing one Ballista does not necessarily mean losing the war.

Becoming the Archenemy"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"People remember Rule of Law. They remember "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Drannith Magistrate"}},{"insert":". They remember "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Aven Mindcensor"}},{"insert":" appearing in response to a tutor. And they definitely remember who was responsible. Accept the attention.
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Being perceived as the problem is often confirmation that the deck is working."},{"insert":"

Patience"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Possibly the most important card in the deck. It just is not printed. Many games are lost by trying to win one turn too early. Many games are won because you waited one turn longer than everyone expected.
You do not need every window. You only need one that stays open.

You Should Play This Deck If..."},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You enjoy being the sheriff at a lawless table.
You like saying “No” without putting a counterspell on the stack.
You prefer timing over speed.
You enjoy turning powerful decks into awkward piles of expensive cardboard.
You believe patience is a resource.
You believe silence is interaction.
And somewhere deep down,
you believe every sufficiently controlled game should eventually be solved by artillery.

One Final Note"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Heliod does not need to race the table.
He needs to make the table slow enough that racing stops mattering.
Let them search.
Let them count mana.
Let them hold interaction.
Let them convince themselves they still have time.
Eventually, somebody taps one land too many.
Casts one spell too early.
Fights the wrong battle.
And when that moment comes, Heliod does not need an army.
He does not need a combat step.
He does not need permission.
He needs one creature.
One window.
One counter to spare.
And one final choice for the table:
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Praise the sun."},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"color":"#ff9900"},"insert":"Or hear the gun."},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"

"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"General Strategy"},{"insert":"
I've opted for an "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"extremely "},{"insert":"greedy version of Baba, attempting to activate her ASAP and to activate her every round, if possible. Rather than building long-term engines, this deck is basically living paycheck-to-paycheck. Solving her 3-type potion puzzle is extremely fun to me, since it keeps me on my toes every turn, making for high variance not just every game but in every single round. 

However, this means sacrificing long-term planning for short-term bursts of value. In this version of a Baba deck, we can't afford to be precious about our game pieces, not even our resources; Baba's regularly eating away at her own mana base to fill in the gaps. Multi-type lands like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Darksteel Citadel"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Urza's Saga"}},{"insert":" aren't just helpful, they're crucial. That means you're banking on drawing some form of land recursion spell with Baba's card velocity. If you lose that bet, then we get to turn 8 with 4 lands while everyone else has built enormous empires. Figuring out how to survive moment-to-moment and get to next turn, while also trying to figure out how you can win  even when you've sacrificed your long-term plans for short-term gain, is one of the most thrilling parts of playing this list.

"},{"insert":"If you don't manage to find a land recursion helper (such as "},{"insert":{"card-link":"World Shaper"}},{"insert":") then you'll have eaten multiple lands and be several mana resources behind everyone else at the exact moment they've all decided to start attacking your larger life total and picking apart your already-sparse board."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Your mana curve is TINY. I think the highest mana cost in the whole deck is 5, or maybe there's 1 card at mana value 6 in there. With the number of lands I feel comfortable eating, casting something for 5 mana could mean that's the only spell I'm playing, not just that turn, but that "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"round. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Related to the tiny mana curve: yes, Baba will draw you a butt-ton of cards. However, sometimes the cards you're drawing are, like, "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Ornithopter"}},{"insert":"s. You'll look threatening by drawing 3 at a time, but that doesn't always mean you'll have actually drawn answers & threats, just that you've drawn enough to get your commander 1 more activation."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Common Rules Errors"},{"insert":"
Baba sometimes trips people up, so here are some common rules clarifications to answer some questions that may still be puzzling for any folks out there:
Using Baba to sacrifice cards with 2 total types (for instance, just an artifact and a creature) does "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"not "},{"insert":"mean she draws 2 and drains for 2. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Baba sacrifices "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"up to "},{"insert":"3 permanents, not "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"exactly "},{"insert":"3 permanents. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Baba can indeed sacrifice herself, and yes, she can sacrifice herself and any Auras she's wearing, like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Kaya's Ghostform"}},{"insert":", and that Ghostform ability will still see the death and proc to bring her back. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":""Snow" is a supertype, not a card type. Sacrificing Snow or Legendary cards doesn't give Baba anything extra. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Ironically, "Kindred" actually "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"is"},{"insert":" a card type, not a supertype like Legendary or Snow. There are weird and annoying rules reasons for this, take it up with Wizards. But yes, if you sacrificed a "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Lignify"}},{"insert":", that counts for 2 types."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Notable Exclusions:"},{"insert":"
Anything that costs 4 or more mana to achieve multiple card types is just too high of a mana cost. Baba is a high-profile target and the linchpin for the whole deck, she can't really wait for us to get our bearings or set up a value engine. I barely feel comfortable with things that cost 3 mana for all 3 card types, even."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Sting, the Glinting Dagger"}},{"insert":": I like the idea here, untapping your commander each round to activate her multiple times. The problem is, you need 3 things to eat every time you activate her. The supply of fuel will drain much faster than you can refill it, so I personally caution against this line of play unless you have a much "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":""Kindred" card types - I'm still tinkering with these, but as of right now, I haven't found many Kindred cards that I'm compelled to put into this list. The most likely candidates would be "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Lignify"}},{"insert":" or "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Bitterblossom"}},{"insert":". A lot of folks have suggested "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Thornbite Staff"}},{"insert":" too, which could be a good final "activate-Baba-multiple-times-for-a-final-burst-of-damage" play, I suppose, but I don't own one and haven't tested it yet, and for now, Bogbeast and other win cons have been more fun for me anyway."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Gloomshrieker"}},{"insert":" it has 2 types, but I don't like exiling it, personally. Could still be worth it."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Fungal Fortitude"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Not Dead After All"}},{"insert":" and other pop-back effects: I want to play more and more of these, though I prefer the ones that bring things back untapped whenever possible, given how strong that interaction can be with ability haste (like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Thousand-Year Elixir"}},{"insert":")."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Silversmote Ghoul"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Sméagol, Helpful Guide"}},{"insert":" - these are super good in theory, and the new "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Moseo, Vein's New Dean"}},{"insert":" is also "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"very "},{"insert":"compelling. However, I try to activate Baba on other peoples' turns rather than on my own, if I can help it, so as to activate cards like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Tragic Slip"}},{"insert":" and mitigate potential aggression when people move to combat and start looking at high life totals. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Ulvenwald Mysteries"}},{"insert":" - I respect the crap out of these types of cards, and I think there's a very reasonable case to play a different version of Baba that makes amazing use of them. I've opted for a version of Baba that starts activations right away and tries to activate her every single round.  This means I'm sacrificing the long-term for the short-term, most regularly by devouring my own lands, in the hope that I'll draw into some recursion spell to get them all back. That's an extremely risky proposition that some Baba players may prefer not to go for. Instead, steady engines like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Ulvenwald Mysteries"}},{"insert":" that supply fodder every turn without compromising your long-term prospects or permanently reducing your resources, and which convert the loss of 1 item into the creation of another item, could be a "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"very "},{"insert":"cool way to build this deck. I respect the crap out of those players, I just went with a greedier and riskier version. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Ashaya, Soul of the Wild"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Biotransference"}},{"insert":" - mass type-changing cards are rad, but Biotransference turned out to be a huge liability (making everything vulnerable to get "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Vandalblast"}},{"insert":"ed, for instance) and Ashaya is a very high-mana card for this deck's curve. I think these would also be good candidates for a more long-term-minded version of Baba. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Bastion of Remembrance"}},{"insert":" and other AOE damage effects: I want my win conditions to be able to point in 1 direction. Plus, some cards, like Bastion, are the kinds of things you end up not wanting to ever eat. I'm trying to be more careful with how many cards I play that I'm truly unwilling to sacrifice."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Lifegain payoffs - I'm strongly considering a few more of these, like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Enduring Tenacity"}},{"insert":" or the new "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Defiling Daemogoth"}},{"insert":", as some alternative win con options. I'm not sold on them here just yet, but there's strong potential."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":{"card-link":"The Gitrog Monster"}},{"insert":" is a "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"strong "},{"insert":"card advantage engine, but it's 5 mana and I'm unwilling to sacrifice it. I'm trying to save my 5+ mana cards that I don't want to eat for my win con slots. I think it's relevant, though, that card advantage is rarely a thing Baba will struggle with (hence why I'm also not running eatable enchantments like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Treacherous Blessing"}},{"insert":" or "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Demonic Lore"}},{"insert":"). There's definitely more to explore here for longer-term versions of the deck, but in general, any backup draw I use, I'd rather be a little cheaper, and be able to work even if Baba can't stick in play (such as "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Braids, Arisen Nightmare"}},{"insert":"). "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Other Game Changers: I currently only have "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Field of the Dead"}},{"insert":" in here, though if I were to include more, "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Glacial Chasm"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Crop Rotation"}},{"insert":" are probably the only others I'd consider. They'd be ludicrously strong here, though, and I already worry I'm punching harder than I should be at this bracket to begin with. I haven't felt the need to play more Game Changers, and this deck is very clearly Bracket 3 even without those other Game Changer signals in the 99. "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"One Final Note:"},{"insert":"
This version of the deck doesn't 100% reflect what I'm currently experimenting with IRL at the moment. After the "},{"attributes":{"link":"https://youtu.be/xupnwElKm7o?si=NBAu1Yb2CmzlxLux"},"insert":"200-card Extra Turns"},{"insert":" episode, I've actually kept Baba in a 200-card paper version, just for kicks. I'm keeping this version up to date with changes I "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"would "},{"insert":"make if I wasn't tinkering and experimenting with this

Knuck if you buck.primer:
{"ops":[{"insert":"Knuck if you Buck"},{"attributes":{"header":1},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
In accordance with the hit 2004 release of Knuck if you Buck, by Crime Mob and Lil' Scrappy. The inspiration of this deck comes from being a gat-totin', pistol-holdin' Enchinda on yo' damn streets. Throwin; them 'bows up at these hoes, they screamin', they bleadin; from they nose. But when we start to swing, we make them Treasas hit the flo'.

This deck is all about combat, getting small creatures out early and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Knuckles the Echidna"}},{"insert":"  as fast as you can to stack treasures. The decks intends to have 2-3 small 1/2 cmc creatures out then knuckles on turn 3/4 (The earlier the better) then every opponent you are able to hit each combat gets you a treasure leading to (hopefully) three treasures a turn. You then want to use these treasure for cards like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Insurrection"}},{"insert":" paired with "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Relentless Assault"}},{"insert":" . You really need those treasures to be able to get to these combos early so dealing combat damage to EVERY opponent each turn with knuckles out is VERY important. 

Some honorable mentions would be cards like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Commander's Plate"}},{"insert":"  this gives knuckles protection from everything  but red AND +3/+3 on his double strike. "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Fury of the Horde"}},{"insert":"  this is an extra combat out of nowhere as long as you have an extra red spell you can discard to cast it for free leading to insurrection + extra combats much faster. "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Professional Face-Breaker"}},{"insert":"  this card is just a second knuckles doubling the amount of tokens you produce each combat if you have face-breaker and knuckles hitting with knuckles alone leads to 4 treasures being made this scales with more creatures leading to TONS OF MANA.

With that in mind I removed a couple cards like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Sol Ring"}},{"insert":"  as it lead to turn 2 knuckles which was able to end games too fast to be fair in bracket three which is what this is intended to be. Without Sol Ring this deck consistently wins turn at or before turn 7 depending on opponents creatures. If they have lots of creatures a steal creature spell + extra combat spell is very good, if they don't have many creatures I assume you're getting a ton of combat value and people die to commander damage or the alternate win condition of knuckles having 30 or more artifacts which is fairly easy with the treasures he generates.

This deck intends to swing often and early to create as many tokens as possible leveraging extra combat steps to get even more attack triggers for even more treasures. In essence we are knucking and bucking. My pod I play with weekly has a ton of graveyard recursion, if your pod does not those cards should be the first removed as there are much better cards to put in their place. In its current state it needs more removal, more 1-2 CMC creatures for attack triggers turn 3-4 with knuckles, and more combat tricks to get around blockers; but who cares, just-

The Unity.author: Us3ful
The Unity.primer:
{"ops":[{"attributes":{"underline":true,"italic":true,"bold":true},"insert":"UNITY - PRAY - FOLLOW"},{"insert":"

Let’s get one thing straight right out of the gate: "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"This deck is "},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"not"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":" trying to be the fastest at the table."},{"insert":" If you want to combo off on turn three, you’re in the wrong lab.

This deck is designed to create board states that shift, mutate, and grow constantly. The goal was to build a deck that actually feels like The Master is running the show. The Unity isn't something you just summon from your hand—it’s something you meticulously build.

This is a Sultai value engine built to flood graveyards, spread radiation, and steal the best threats on the board. With "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Master, Transcendent"},{"insert":" running the show, your goal is to mill yourself and your opponents, then tap The Master to snatch freshly milled creatures and turn them into 3/3 green Mutants. You back this up with rad counters, +1/+1 counter synergies, and classic mill payoffs. We aren't looking for infinite combos here; we win through grinding attrition, radioactive drain, and overwhelming board states.

The Game Plan"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Early Game: Prime the Pump"},{"insert":" 
Ramp hard and start milling early. Drop your mana dorks and rocks alongside cheap mill engines like "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Ruin Crab"},{"insert":" or "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Mesmeric Orb"},{"insert":". You want those graveyards overflowing by the time you reach the mid-game.

"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Mid Game: Harvest and Mutate"},{"insert":" 
Cast The Master and start harvesting. Remember, he only grabs creatures milled "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"this turn"},{"insert":", so sequence your mill effects right before you tap him. Start layering your board with draw engines, counter multipliers like "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Hardened Scales"},{"insert":", and your Mutant lords to turn your 3/3s into massive threats.

Closing the Game"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You have a few ways to cross the finish line:
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Mill:"},{"insert":" Wipe out their libraries entirely with "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Phenax, God of Deception"},{"insert":" or "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Court of Cunning"},{"insert":"."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Drain:"},{"insert":" Bleed the table dry using "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Syr Konrad, the Grim"},{"insert":" paired with "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Mindcrank"},{"insert":"."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Beatdown:"},{"insert":" Turn your oversized, radioactive Mutants sideways and swing for lethal."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Backup Plan:"},{"insert":" If The Master gets hated out, "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Muldrotha, the Gravetide"},{"insert":" steps in to keep the graveyard train rolling."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Pro Tips for Piloting"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Timing is everything."},{"insert":" Always trigger your mill "},{"attributes":{"italic":true},"insert":"before"},{"insert":" activating The Master so you actually have legal targets to steal."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Tyvar is your best friend."},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler"},{"insert":" lets you use The Master the turn he comes down and untaps him for double the stealing."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Maximize your proliferate."},{"insert":" Hold your proliferate spells until you have multiple targets online. Grow your rad counters, +1/+1 counters, and planeswalkers all at once for maximum value."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Watch your library."},{"insert":" Keep "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Elixir of Immortality"},{"insert":" handy so you do not accidentally deck yourself under your own heavy self-mill."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The All-Stars"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Enablers:"},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Mesmeric Orb"},{"insert":" and "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Ruin Crab"},{"insert":" fill the yards passively and pressure the whole table."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Drainers:"},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Syr Konrad, the Grim"},{"insert":" and "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Mindcrank"},{"insert":" turn every milled card and point of damage into a nightmare for your opponents."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Multipliers:"},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Hardened Scales"},{"insert":", "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Corpsejack Menace"},{"insert":", and "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Wise Mothman"},{"insert":" turn your baseline 3/3 Mutants into terrifying beaters."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"The Closers:"},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Phenax, God of Deception"},{"insert":" and "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Altar of Dementia"},{"insert":" let you pivot to a direct mill finish if the red zone is stalled."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
